releasesInRange.body:
## New Features

- Added keyboard-driven transcript selection with word, line, and page motions, integrated search, and configurable shortcuts. (#57221, #57222, #57223, #57224)
- Rendered Markdown consistently in async questions, choices, answers, and transcript replies. (#57259, #57292)
- Added GPT-6.1 Terra to the bundled, Vertex AI, and Amazon Bedrock model catalogs. (#57293)
- Added `codex queue --resume` to resume unloaded threads after queueing a message. (#57232)
- Added clearer safety-block explanations and selectable safer follow-up prompts in the TUI. (#57363, #57365)
- Added `codex doctor --network-only` for focused configuration, connectivity, and WebSocket diagnostics. (#57606)

## Bug Fixes

- Preserved acknowledged approval and permission settings when resuming or forking threads. (#57227)
- Preserved local image attachments when restoring killed composer text. (#57502)
- Fixed standalone release cleanup on macOS when installations are in use or paths contain non-ASCII characters. (#57503)
- Restored spawned descendant threads when unarchiving their parent. (#57635)
- Fixed app-server thread startup and shutdown races and released completed runtimes promptly. (#57787, #57788)
- Improved TUI reconnection recovery, including offline `/quit` and `/exit` handling. (#57820)
- Preserved reasoning-token accounting across resume and fork to avoid premature compaction. (#57839)

## Chores

- Switched Bazel to source-built V8 with target-matched Rust bindings and native Windows MSVC archive support. (#57164, #57269, #57644, #57832)
- Shipped the standalone executor in canonical CLI and app-server release packages. (#57837)
- Standardized development and release builds on Node.js 24.22.1 and Rust 1.95.0. (#57168, #57373)

## Changelog

Full Changelog: https://github.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.165.0...rust-v0.166.0

- #56505 Defer synchronous Guardian tool-call truncation to preparation @ioanbudea-OAI
- #56514 Preserve tracing context throughout tool dispatch @bkotsopoulos

- #56516 Respect server approval policy defaults during TUI startup @etraut-openai
- #56524 Add turn, tool, and skill attribution to traces @bkotsopoulos

prs.title: Add `codex doctor --network-only` for focused network diagnostics
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add `codex doctor --network-only` for focused network diagnostics

## What changed

Limit `--network-only` reports to effective configuration, network environment, provider HTTP reachability, and Responses WebSocket checks, skipping unrelated diagnostics such as database and MCP scans. Preserve configuration warnings and report configuration load timing.

If configuration loading fails, report the redacted configuration error and stop without probing guessed network targets.

## Testing

Add integration tests for check selection, recoverable configuration warnings, and configuration failures that send no probe requests or expose configuration values. Add snapshots for human-readable success and failure reports.

prs.title: Share runtime authentication with model providers and catalogs
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Share runtime authentication with model providers and catalogs

## Why

Model catalog refreshes need to use the same registered actor and credential owner as model requests when runtime authentication is enabled.

## What changed

- Add `ProviderAuthContext` to carry credentials and optional runtime authentication into model providers and catalog clients.
- Select runtime authentication independently for inference and catalog destinations. Reject unsupported OpenAI origins while preserving provider authentication for other destinations.
- Include API organization and project selectors in runtime registration. Reuse registered runtimes across projects within an organization and replace them when the organization changes.
- Preserve transport restrictions and account bindings, and strip sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects.
- Apply the catalog timeout to authentication and fetching while allowing credential refresh and registration to finish safely.

## Testing

Add coverage for runtime-authenticated catalogs, provider isolation, resource selection, gateway authentication, cross-origin redirects, and timeout recovery that preserves registration and refreshed tokens.

prs.title: Disable terminal status sequences on older VTE backends
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Disable terminal status sequences on older VTE backends

## Why

VTE versions before 0.54 lack the parser that safely ignores unknown OSC sequences. Terminal status reporting needs to account for the VTE backend even when the terminal identifies itself as GNOME Terminal or another application.

## What changed

- Track VTE backend versions independently of terminal application identity.
- Disable `OSC 7501` and `OSC 21337` status reporting when the detected VTE version is below 0.54. Preserve existing behavior for newer or unknown versions.
- Prefer `VTE_VERSION` over the terminal application version, treating empty or malformed values as unknown.

## Testing

Add regression tests for GNOME identity with VTE metadata, version precedence, and status protocol selection around the VTE 0.54 boundary, including unknown versions.

prs.title: Preserve rollout tracing across sub-agent reloads
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve rollout tracing across sub-agent reloads

## Why

Reloading an evicted sub-agent disabled its rollout tracing, leaving later turns out of the trace. Replacement Code Mode sessions could also reuse cell IDs from earlier sessions.

## What changed

- Reattach reloaded children to the root rollout trace and emit `ThreadResumed` without duplicating `ThreadStarted`.
- Reopen existing threads during replay, preserving their identity and history while clearing stale runtime cell and terminal process mappings.
- Allocate Code Mode cell generations across sessions for both gRPC and stdio hosts to prevent ID reuse after reload.
- Record an aborted trace when session startup fails before the session loop begins.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for child eviction and reload, including a failed reload, continued inference tracing, distinct cell IDs, and preserved mail and follow-up context. Extend replay tests for history preservation and reused runtime handles, and host tests for cell IDs across session replacement and reconnection.

prs.title: Release sampling prompts after stream setup
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Release sampling prompts after stream setup

## Why

Legacy notifications only need user text, but retaining the full sampling input keeps image and audio payloads alive while the response streams.

## What changed

Extract notification text from the first request attempt only when `notify` is configured, and retain those strings across retries. Consume and drop the prompt after setting up the response stream, excluding attachments and media wrapper labels from notification text.

## Testing

Extend the notification integration test to verify that `input-messages` contains only user text while the model request still includes image and audio attachments.

prs.title: Show Bedrock setup for explicitly configured OpenAI providers
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Show Bedrock setup for explicitly configured OpenAI providers

## Why

Setting `model_provider = "openai"` hid the Amazon Bedrock setup option during onboarding, even though leaving the provider implicit allowed it.

## What changed

Allow the Bedrock setup wizard when the effective provider is `openai`, whether selected explicitly or by default. Preserve the existing feature, authentication, login-method, and embedded app-server requirements.

## Testing

Update onboarding tests to cover explicit OpenAI configuration, continued exclusion of custom providers, and the Bedrock sign-in option with configuration loaded from `config.toml`.

prs.title: Stop shipping `codex-exec-server` in release artifacts
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stop shipping `codex-exec-server` in release artifacts

## What changed

- Remove the standalone executor from CLI and app-server packages, release binary lists, and Bazel runtime archives.
- Remove the package builder's `--exec-server-bin` option and `execServer` metadata, along with executor-specific installer checks, signing configuration, and package smoke tests.
- Keep the standalone executor available to build from source.

prs.title: Restore spawned descendants when unarchiving a thread
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Restore spawned descendants when unarchiving a thread

## Why

Archiving a thread also archives its spawned descendants, but unarchiving it previously restored only the parent.

## What changed

- Restore archived spawned descendants when handling `thread/unarchive`, including descendants archived independently of the parent. Skip active descendants and continue past descendant restoration failures; fall back to restoring only the parent if descendant discovery fails.
- Emit `thread/unarchived` for each successfully restored thread. Hold the thread-list mutation permit through archive and unarchive responses and notifications to preserve ordering with other list mutations.
- Add `ThreadStore::unarchive_threads` and share rollout discovery across the subtree in the local store.

## Testing

Extend coverage for subtree restoration, independently archived children, descendant restoration failures, and failed descendant discovery. Store tests cover skipping active descendants and restoring archived descendants without hydrating their metadata.

prs.title: Add OpenTelemetry requirement types to the app-server protocol
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add OpenTelemetry requirement types to the app-server protocol

## What changed

Add optional `otel` requirements to `ConfigRequirements`, with types for logging controls, tool-result byte limits, environment, and telemetry exporters, including OTLP HTTP/gRPC headers and TLS settings.

Update the JSON schemas, precomputed exports, and generated TypeScript and Python bindings. The app-server requirements mapper currently returns `otel: None`.

prs.title: Generate Rust bindings that match Bazel-built V8 archives
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Generate Rust bindings that match Bazel-built V8 archives

## Why

Pre-generated bindings can disagree with native V8 layouts, including CppGC member storage and the inline typed-array size. Source archives need bindings generated with the same headers, defines, and target configuration.

## What changed

- Generate bindings through Bazel using the archive's C++ compilation metadata, and include them in Darwin and Linux release pairs and source builds.
- Select native Windows MSVC archives and matching bindings together with `--//:rusty_v8_from_source=true`, and generate target-specific Windows GNU bindings.
- Pin a corrected `rusty_v8` revision for Cargo and Bazel, and track native Windows LLVM tools and resources as action inputs so pin changes invalidate cached actions.
- Run release and canary Cargo smoke tests with explicit target triples, required Linux linkers, and `--include-ignored`.

## Testing

Add `codex-v8-poc` coverage for CppGC member size, alignment, tracing, and weak references; typed-array contents and backing-store promotion; and microtask queues across garbage collection and context reassignment. Enable the otherwise ignored CppGC ABI checks for Bazel source builds and staged release smoke tests.

prs.title: Support managed OpenTelemetry configuration requirements
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support managed OpenTelemetry configuration requirements

## What changed

- Allow `requirements.toml` to manage OpenTelemetry logging flags, tool-result byte limits, environment, and log, trace, and metrics exporters.
- Apply higher-priority managed values over user configuration, replacing exporters atomically and warning when configured values conflict. Preserve unmanaged settings, including `span_attributes` and `tracestate`.
- Expose managed `otel` settings through `configRequirements/read`, apply them in `config/read` without ordinary field origins, and reject configuration writes that overlap managed fields.
- Distinguish omitted tool-result limits from explicit values while preserving the runtime default.

## Testing

Add coverage for requirement precedence, relative TLS paths, override warnings, managed write protection, effective configuration reads, and exporter serialization through the app-server API.

prs.title: Redact OTEL exporter headers in app-server config responses
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Redact OTEL exporter headers in app-server config responses

## Why

OTEL exporter headers can contain credentials. Configuration responses exposed these values in effective config, source layers, managed requirements, and write-override metadata.

## What changed

Replace header values with `[redacted]` across these responses for log, trace, and metrics exporters while preserving header names. Keep the original values available to runtime exporters, and redact them in debug output. Update protocol schemas and generated client documentation to describe the redacted values.

## Testing

Add coverage for effective config and source-layer redaction, managed requirements, and single and batch write-override metadata, including header names containing dots. Extend telemetry integration coverage to verify that runtime requests still carry the configured header value.

prs.title: Fix trace exporter activation after account switches
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix trace exporter activation after account switches

## Why

When the app server started with tracing disabled, its subscriber lacked the trace bridge needed to export spans after an account switch enabled tracing. Disabling tracing also left the previous global tracer provider installed.

## What changed

- Always install the reloadable trace layer so account switches can enable trace export without restarting the app server.
- Replace the global tracer provider with a no-op provider when trace export is disabled, including when all telemetry exporters are disabled.

## Testing

Add an app-server regression test that starts with tracing disabled, enables a requirements-managed trace exporter on account switch, and verifies export with the parent trace ID preserved. Add a provider unit test verifying that disabling telemetry stops new spans from recording.

prs.title: Support managed OpenTelemetry metadata and PEM client identities
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support managed OpenTelemetry metadata and PEM client identities

## Why

Managed OpenTelemetry requirements could not specify span attributes or tracestate metadata.

## What changed

- Accept `otel.span_attributes` and `otel.tracestate` in requirements, merge them by attribute or member field, and expose them through app-server configuration and requirements reads.
- Protect required entries and their ancestors from configuration writes while preserving unmanaged sibling values and their origins. For example, requiring `otel.tracestate.vendor.tenant` leaves `vendor.region` writable. Empty metadata maps impose no requirements.
- Select Rustls when configuring an OTLP HTTP client certificate and private key so PEM client identities are accepted.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata precedence, effective configuration, field-level write protection, and preservation of unmanaged values. Add blocking and asynchronous HTTP client construction tests using generated PEM certificates and keys.

prs.title: Remove detached delivery from `review/start`
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Remove detached delivery from `review/start`

## What changed

`review/start` now supports only inline reviews on the supplied thread and returns that thread's id as `reviewThreadId`. Clients can omit `delivery`, send `null`, or specify `"inline"`; `"detached"` is no longer supported.

For a separate review thread, call `thread/start` followed by `review/start`. To preserve conversation history with custom review instructions, use `thread/fork` followed by `turn/start`.

Remove detached review execution and its app-server dependency on `codex-agent-extension`, and update the protocol schemas and generated clients. Preserve `ReviewDelivery.inline` as a Python enum member.

## Testing

Add a Python regression test verifying that inline review delivery parses as `ReviewDelivery.inline` and round-trips to the original JSON.

prs.title: Preserve parent routing affinity for Guardian reviews
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve parent routing affinity for Guardian reviews

## Why

Shared routing cookies can change after a parent connection is established. Guardian reviews need the routing affinity captured with their parent response so unrelated traffic does not replace that hint.

## What changed

- Capture `__oailb` and `__cflb` cookies from successful ChatGPT WebSocket handshakes and pair them with the parent response ID.
- Retain the snapshot throughout a review and its retries, and apply it only to Guardian requests with the matching parent response. Reconnect cached reviewer sockets when the parent affinity changes.
- Preserve cookie expiry and restrict reuse to the original secure origin and endpoint path. Replace routing cookies while retaining unrelated cookies, and keep the captured affinity out of prompts, history, and serialized metadata.

## Testing

Add coverage for cookie scope, expiry, duplicate rejection, and merging; replaying a captured pin after shared cookies change or are deleted; and retaining the matching parent snapshot through compaction without exposing cookies in review prompts or metadata.

## Testing

reviewer crate, preserving coverage for input, Windows working directories, and
sandbox permission modes.

prs.title: Disable optimization for the on-demand Bazel schema generator
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Disable optimization for the on-demand Bazel schema generator

## Why

The short-lived schema exporter sits on the critical path of application builds. Optimizing its full test harness adds unnecessary compilation work.

## What changed

Compile `schema-generator-on-demand` with `-Copt-level=0` and keep debug assertions disabled with `-Cdebug-assertions=no`, preserving exec-mode assertion behavior.

prs.title: Expose Guardian assessments in response streams
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Expose Guardian assessments in response streams

## What changed

Decode `response.metadata` Guardian assessments into typed `GuardianAssessment` events over SSE and WebSocket, carrying `response_id`, `item_id`, and `requires_review`. Ignore assessments with missing, empty, or incorrectly typed required fields while preserving independent delivery of other metadata.

Expose the assessment type to request-scoped extension interceptors. Keep assessments out of conversation history; they do not authorize tool execution.

## Testing

Add SSE coverage for assessment ordering, malformed metadata, and mixed metadata delivery. Extend model request tests to cover SSE and WebSocket interceptor delivery and exclusion from subsequent model input.

Fix app-server thread listener startup and shutdown races
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix app-server thread listener startup and shutdown races

## Why

A thread runtime can shut down while listener setup is awaiting I/O, and a cold resume can start before the previous listener forwards `ShutdownComplete`. Listener replacement must preserve those buffered terminal events.

## What changed

- Coordinate listener installation and connection subscriptions with pending unloads, and reject closing or replaced runtimes.
- Allow a newly created runtime that has already shut down to drain its queued events, while enforcing one event reader per runtime.
- Track shutdown draining with a shared watch channel so cold resume and runtime replacement wait for terminal events to be processed.
- Serialize idle unloading with goal edits and cold resume, and recheck thread state after acquiring the lock.
